acceptance: Secret plaintext never appears in SQLite rows, Event payloads, logs, prompts, process arguments, sandbox environments, or artifact exports.
A secret handle is an opaque non-secret identifier that authorizes nothing by possession; only broker admission under an exact Grant can produce a bounded resolved use.
secret.use is admitted only for one exact secret reference and one exact approved destination class and never implies secret.reveal.
Provider adapters declare exact identity and capabilities and fail closed on unknown, unavailable, or malformed provider responses.
The OS credential-store adapter reaches the platform store only through a fixed non-shell command template, and native library binding remains explicitly deferred.
Adversarial tests prove that cross-destination handle reuse, unapproved destinations, provider spoofing, and redaction failure are denied and that no plaintext leaks.
Existing S05-T01 and S05-T02 policy, profile, store, and daemon authorization behavior and the SQLite policy schema are unchanged.
The original tracked ContextSource and WorkPacket files are generated before implementation, replay byte-identically through the pinned CLI, and remain immutable execution-authority evidence.

Exact-head implementation passes full pnpm check, Diffcipline R3, Alibaba OpenCodeReview accounting, native macOS qualification, six-job CI, review with zero unresolved threads, ordinary merge, and six-job post-merge qualification.
Native SpecGrain verification binds the exact original WorkPacket to independently observed implementation evidence with every acceptance and evidence item satisfied before closeout.
Canonical closeout advances only KX-P02-S06-T01 after proof and P02 phase exit remains unproven.

minimality.rationale: Reuse existing Grants, consequence classification, policy envelopes, store and Event machinery, and daemon authorization. Add one dependency-free crate plus its workspace membership; no new external dependency, KMS, schema, or provider-specific permission model.

requirements: Plaintext secret values must never be persisted, logged, prompted, placed in process arguments or environments, or exported as artifacts.
A handle must never be a bearer credential; possession alone must authorize nothing.
Unknown, unavailable, or malformed provider responses must fail closed rather than degrade to plaintext or to a default provider.
secret.reveal must remain a distinct C3 capability that this Grain does not grant.
Do not start implementation until the original ContextSource and WorkPacket are durably tracked and exact replay is proven.
Do not advance S06-T02 or P02 exit until S06-T01 native proof and canonical closeout are complete.

outcome: Implement a repository-owned, provider-neutral secret broker that identifies secrets by opaque Kernux handle instead of plaintext, admits bounded secret.use only for one exact approved destination through a declared provider adapter, and keeps plaintext out of SQLite, events, logs, process arguments, prompts, and artifact export.
rationale: KX-P02-S05-T02 is PROVEN and post-merge-qualified. The canonical security model requires secrets to be referenced and brokered rather than copied, with plaintext-at-rest in an OS credential store or approved provider, domain-scoped use, redaction, and auditability. This macro task is the dependency-eligible next P02 unit.

risk.recovery: Revert only SG-000026 secret-broker changes and keep KX-P02-S06-T01 at NEXT. Preserve existing policy, profile, store, and daemon semantics, the tracked WorkPacket evidence, and the canonical ledgers; never store plaintext and never advance S06-T02 on failed secret proof.

scope_in: Add a repository-owned dependency-free kernux-secret crate that models opaque non-secret secret handles, canonical secret references, declared provider adapters, and a bounded broker admission path.

Keep plaintext out of SQLite, events, logs, prompts, process arguments, sandbox environments, and artifact export; persist only references, handle identity, provider identity, destination class, and redaction metadata.

Admit secret.use only for one exact secret reference and one exact approved destination class under one exact Run and optional AgentSession, one exact Runtime revision, finite trusted windows, a positive finite max_uses, and existing Grant validation plus mandatory authority intersection.

Model first-generation OS credential-store adapters behind one provider trait and reach the platform credential store only through the daemon brokered process authority with a fixed non-shell command template.
Keep secret.reveal as a distinct C3 capability that no preset profile and no broker default grants automatically.
Add adversarial tests for plaintext leakage, cross-destination handle reuse, unapproved destinations, unknown providers, malformed provider responses, and redaction failure paths.
Persist the original SpecGrain ContextSource set and WorkPacket bytes before the first implementation slice and require byte-identical replay.

Qualify every bounded implementation slice with full pnpm check, Diffcipline R3, Alibaba OpenCodeReview accounting, native macOS qualification, exact-head six-job CI, semantic review with zero unresolved threads, ordinary merge, and exact post-merge six-job qualification.
scope_out: Do not add new external dependencies in this Grain; native credential-store library bindings are deferred to a governed dependency-admission Grain.
Do not implement approval UI, organization or team secret sharing, secret rotation UX, or the HTTP egress substitution broker.
Do not store plaintext secrets and do not add KRP fields, core actions, resource authorities, consequence classes, or provider-specific permission models.
Do not auto-grant secret.reveal, do not treat a handle as a bearer credential, and do not add a hidden global secret-access switch.
Do not advance KX-P02-S06-T02 or P02 phase exit from implementation evidence alone.
title: KX-P02-S06-T01 — Implement secret-provider abstraction and first OS credential-store adapters with handle-based use
